**Stable, published under the npm `latest` dist-tag.** 0.5.1 is 0.5.0 with
one fix in the compiler it embeds: the source nesting limit counts every
`opt` and `vec` until its operand ends. Until 1.0, any release may change the
CLI grammar, the library API, and the request/response shapes. Pin an exact
version.

`@candid-core/schema` 0.3 breaks the 0.2 API (principal values are canonical text, collapsing opts are boxed, every `vec nat8` is a `Uint8Array`, generated modules use a new binding layout and may omit declarations, and the `./actor`, `./transport-icp`, `./forms` and `./labels` subpaths are gone); there is no compatibility layer.

That line is the 0.3 line's, unchanged. What this release changes against
0.5.0 is below: which sources the nesting limit refuses, and how.

## Installation

```sh
npm install --save-exact @meantjs/schema@0.6.0
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @meantjs/cli@0.5.1
npx @meantjs/cli@0.5.1 gen ./service.did -o ./generated
```

The command the package installs is `meant`, so a script in `package.json`
calls `meant gen …`. Never run a bare `npx meant`: the unscoped `meant`
package on npm belongs to another author, so where this package is not
installed, npx would offer to download and run that one. `npx @meantjs/cli`
always names this package. In a shell, a bare `meant` runs whichever `meant`
comes first on the `PATH`, which can be the Rust compiler's binary from
`cargo install meant`, whose commands are `compile` and `validate`; a script
in `package.json` puts this package's command first.

## What an app on 0.5.0 does

1. Install this release with the second line above. The peer is still
   exactly `@meantjs/schema` `0.6.0`, so the schema stays as it is.
2. Nothing else. Wherever both releases compile a source, they write the
   same module and envelope byte for byte (measured below), so
   `meant gen --check` keeps passing over the modules 0.5.0 wrote.
3. A script that reads the `--json` failure documents may see resource
   `source_nesting` where 0.5.0 reported `type_depth`, and
   `resource_limit_exceeded` where 0.5.0 failed with `internal_error`; the
   table below has both cases.

## Pairing

- **Peer**: `@meantjs/schema` at exactly `0.6.0` (optional), as in 0.5.0.
  No schema release comes with this one.
- **Embedded revision**: `meant` 0.1.0 and the `meant-ts` generator, both
  compiled from the commit the release is dispatched from; the run records
  the SHA. The generator is the one 0.5.0 embedded as `candid-core-ts`; since
  then its source has changed in comments and in that name only. The
  dispatched commit's `meant` source is ahead of the crates.io 0.1.0 archive
  (published from commit `56186e17be6c405beb51f01b0ece5fdc7ff150a2`) by
  three changes, none of which moves a Contract or an identity: the doc
  attributes reader (#279) and type-depth walks keyed on visit order (#263),
  which 0.5.0 embedded already, and the source nesting count (#337), which
  is this release's fix. The envelopes' `producer` reads `meant` `0.1.0`, as
  in 0.5.0.
- **Not released with it**: the `meant` crate. crates.io stays on 0.1.0; no
  crate release is needed first, since no Contract or identity moved. The
  root changelog records the three changes under `## Unreleased` for the
  next crate release.

## Against 0.5.0, measured

With this release's packed tarball against the registry's 0.5.0 (Node
22.23.4, Linux x64), each source run through `gen --json` alone from its own
directory:

- On the repository's 44 tracked `.did` files outside `profile/`, both
  releases compile the same 40 and refuse the same 4, with the same exit
  status and byte-identical `--json` output, and the 40 modules and 40
  envelopes are byte-identical.
- On sources built to sit at the limit, each one declaration `T` beside
  `service : {}` (the last beside `service : { f : (T) -> () }`):

| Source | Bytes | 0.5.0 | 0.5.1 |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 256 nested `record`, the innermost `record {}` at type depth 255 | 3 859 | written | written, byte-identical |
| 257 nested `record`, the innermost at type depth 256 | 3 874 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 | written |
| 258 nested `record` | 3 889 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 |
| 257 nested `variant`, the innermost `variant {}` at type depth 256 | 4 131 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 | written |
| 258 nested `variant` | 4 147 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 |
| 257 nested `func`, the innermost `func () -> ()` at type depth 256 | 3 366 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 | written |
| 258 nested `func` | 3 379 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 |
| `vec` × 256 around `record {}` | 1 058 | written | written, byte-identical |
| `vec` × 257 around `record {}` | 1 062 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 | refused: `source_nesting` 257 |
| 64 levels of `vec vec vec record { a : …`, then `nat` at type depth 256 | 1 755 | written | written, byte-identical |
| the same with `opt nat`, at type depth 257 | 1 759 | refused after parsing: `type_depth` 257 | refused before parsing: `source_nesting` 257 |
| 256 levels, the one at depth d a run of 256 − d `vec` before `record { a : …`, 33 152 levels in all | 135 467 | failed: `internal_error`, "Maximum call stack size exceeded" | refused: `source_nesting` 257 |

A refusal is `resource_limit_exceeded` with limit 256, and the number after
the resource is the `observed` value. Every written entry exits 0, and every
refusal or failure exits 1.

## Public API against 0.5.0

The previous stable release, compared with the registry's tarball itself
(`npm pack @meantjs/cli@0.5.0`; its SHA-512 equals
`npm view @meantjs/cli@0.5.0 dist.integrity`,
`sha512-Q3iqiiYuF2XKU4aMBiFvkn/QGoH178EsxKNCAOyyz20TbC7n8vChEGzXF6yf6LTG5nniKAJ2i8eoBBOOZUktow==`,
and its `gitHead` is `1f0cfe8946f75eca0cbfa32d178ec7052f45dfd7`), against
this release packed from the prepared commit. Nothing breaks.

Both tarballs hold the same nine files. Of the code, only the wasm module
differs (1 959 675 bytes in 0.5.0, 1 959 468 in 0.5.1), because it embeds
the new count:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/index.d.ts`, `lib/index.js` | none, byte-identical: every exported name keeps its declaration (32 names) |
| `bin/cli.js` | none, byte-identical: `gen`, `project` and `check` keep their flags and exit codes, and the `--json` documents keep `schemaVersion` `1` |
| `wasm/candid_core_wasm.js` | none, byte-identical |
| `wasm/candid_core_wasm_bg.wasm` | the compiler with the new source nesting count |
| `package.json` | `version`; `repository.directory` and `homepage` name `crates/meant-wasm/npm`, where they named `crates/candid-core-wasm/npm` |

Generated modules: unchanged. The generator is 0.5.0's, and wherever both
releases compile a source, the module and envelope are byte-identical
(above).

## Known limitations and deferred work

- An entry named through a file symlink, or in another case on a
  case-insensitive file system, fails with `did_source_not_found` (#251).
- Doc comments above a quoted name (`"foo-bar" : …`) are not recorded by the
  pinned `candid_parser` 0.4.0, so `didToDocAttributes` sees no docs there.
- The multi-entry bundle-root rule and the duplicate-stem refusal apply the
  issue's recommendations and may be revisited before 1.0 (#193).
- Two structurally equal record declarations still collapse to the first
  name (#197, "Not yet scheduled"), and declarations whose records
  canonicalize to one node share its field names (#229).
- The embedded `meant` is not byte-identical to the crates.io 0.1.0 archive
  (above). The native `meant` 0.1.0 counts source nesting as 0.5.0 does; the
  next crate release carries all three changes.

## Irreversibility

An npm name and version are permanent: once published, a version can be
deprecated, but never republished with other bytes. The wasm in the tarball
is built in the release job with the pinned release toolchain and
`wasm-pack`, so its bytes are those two pins applied to the dispatched
commit.
